title: Boundary of the Four Spirits
text: “How badly were Yuki-chan and the others hurt?”
When my Father asked that, both the Assistant and Yuki-chan looked away.
“We managed to defeat it, but the familiar’s attacks were fierce, and there are many casualties…”
Come to think of it, everyone’s a mess. The only ones without any injuries are me and my Father. That’s how difficult the mission was.
“So, just when I thought the Spirit Tortoise was dead… that Spirit Tortoise turned into a faint light and vanished.”
“It vanished into light…?”
“Come to think of it…”
I look around. There’s not a single trace of the Dragon King’s corpse, which should have been there just a moment ago.
“…There was a corpse when we defeated the Qilin too, but it disappeared after that light passed through.”
“The Phoenix too.”
My father fell deep in thought.
“By the way, Father, when I loop back into my field of vision, the spear I’m holding—the effect of the Minute Hand of the Dragon Hourglass—shows an icon for ‘Branching Worlds.’”
“Huh?”
I explained to my father the icon and options appearing in my field of vision, as well as the remaining time that was gradually decreasing.
“That… Ah, I think I might know why now.”
“What do you mean?”

My Father covered his face with his hands in an exasperated tone. The Queen rushed over and asked him, “What is it?” My Father really knows his stuff, doesn’t he? My Finacée and the Lazy Pig are also looking around nervously.
“Probably… we failed to defeat the Four Spirits.”
“W-what do you mean? We definitely defeated them.”
“Well, I mean, we were half-successful in defeating the Four Spirits themselves… but before we could do that, their objective was already fulfilled.”
“I’d like you to explain that in detail.”
“So here’s the thing. By sacrificing two-thirds of the world’s life, they create a barrier to protect the world from the Wave. The Spirit Tortoise accomplished that objective—with its final blow.”
My father explained it as if a single drop of water falling onto the brim of a cup already filled to the brim would cause it to overflow.
“Are you trying to say it’s my fault?”
“No, that’s not it. Either way, I think it was a close call. It’s entirely possible they sacrificed the souls of the Four Spirits themselves…”
My father let out a deep sigh. Indeed, that gigantic Spirit Tortoise… no, the Four Spirits themselves would likely be able to make up for the shortfall.

“Come to think of it, the arrival time for the next wave isn’t showing up in my field of vision. I suppose this means that, even though we’ve suffered such immense losses, the world has been saved from the threat of the waves?”
“All’s well that ends well—but it doesn’t quite work that way,” my father said resignedly.
“So, what’s appearing in your field of vision, Motoyasu-kun… is this it? The choice—‘Is this okay?’—and the time you have to make it.”
“So, if I choose ‘Yes,’ the loop will end, right?”
“Probably.”
“Then I’ll make my choice.”
“Wait a second!”
Just as I was about to make my choice, my father stepped forward and called out to me.
“What’s the matter?”
“There’s no way this ending could be good! Two-thirds of the world has been lost, you know?”
“But the danger of being threatened by the waves is gone.”
“Motoyasu, you don’t remember how you ended up in this loop… you only remember losing in the future, right?”
I nod. I do have a vague memory of being defeated by someone, but I don’t remember the details.

“I don’t think it led to the same outcome as this ending, but it’s not impossible either. I want you to look further into the future. Somewhere down the line, the world might have been exposed to an unstoppable threat.”
Hearing that, I start to feel like he might be right. But… I still have this vague feeling that I was defeated by the waves?
“Besides, what was your original goal, Motoyasu-kun? It was to meet that Filolial named Philo, who’s going to become my daughter, right?”
“I’ll look for her in a world where peace has been restored.”
“If you can really believe that little girl Filo-tan’s egg is safe after all this destruction… that’s something else…”

Good heavens! It certainly sounds like finding Filo-tan will be a real struggle. No, maybe Filo-tan is even among the victims of the Four Spirits. That would be absolutely terrible. Ah, if time could be rewound, I’d really want it to be.
“Looks like you’ve finally figured it out. Anyway, there’s no way this ending is acceptable.”
“You’re right.”
“Probably… the final choice is up to Motoyasu-kun, and if he chooses ‘No,’ time will rewind… I’d like to think so, at least.”
I see. That’s certainly a strong possibility. So what should I do, then? Which should I choose—a world without turmoil or Filo-tan?!
“No way… So, does that mean all our hard work has gone down the drain!?”
“Huh… No, I don’t want that!”
Keel and his Finacée both shook their heads. My future Father bent down to meet Keel and his Finacée’s gaze.
“Keel, even if we rebuild the village… with this many casualties, who knows what will become of the village’s survivors?”
“…But…”
“Of course, if—”
“If everything were to be erased, would I forget about Naofumi-sama? Would these feelings… just disappear?”
The Finacée furrows her brow and asks, as if seeking salvation.
“That’s… true. But—”
“Bububu—!”
The Lazy Pig is babbling something nonstop as if it’s gone berserk. The people around them look a bit annoyed.

“Elena, even if you say you’d rather die than let it all be erased just because you bet on the winning horse, do you realize how much effort it’ll take to recover from all this damage? It’s definitely going to take way longer than just a few years, isn’t it?”
My father stood up and addressed the people around him, asking them to let him continue.
“Just because Motoyasu chose ‘No’ doesn’t mean everything will rewind. It might be that only Motoyasu… jumps forward in time. If that happens, I think we’ll have to go on living in this world.”
“If that happens, Gaelion will do my best alongside my big sister! I’ll live on as the next Dragon Emperor!”
“The Dragon Emperor’s shards… they’ve vanished, after all.”
“There’s a reaction! The Dragon King must have spat them out at the very end! Let’s go find them and gather them up!”
“Yeah, you’re right. If the King of Monsters cooperates, the world’s recovery might go faster.”
“……I tried my best, but it didn’t work out…… I’m sorry. If I hadn’t hit the Sword Hero, this wouldn’t have happened……”
The assistant is trembling uncontrollably. Father gently hugs her.
“……It’s not your fault, Wyndia. So don’t be so hard on yourself. It was our fault for failing to persuade Ren and Itsuki and stop them.”
“But……”

“Besides, even if you hadn’t hit them, Wyndia-chan, Ren and Itsuki probably would’ve broken the Phoenix’s seal anyway. They probably thought Motoyasu and I were keeping an eye on the Spirit Tortoise. So why don’t you focus on what comes next?”
Gently, her father placed his index finger against the assistant’s nose as he spoke. Moved by his kindness, the assistant wiped away her tears and nodded.
“Well then, Motoyasu, what should we do next? We don’t have much time, do we? Let’s do what we can right now.”
“Is there something forming in your mind, Father?”
“Not yet… Maybe it’ll come to me after Motoyasu makes his choice. Like, whether or not to return to the original world?”

Wow, it’s a bit of an unpleasant ending, but does this mean Father will be able to return to the original world after all? My future Father said he was fighting to return to his original world. Does that mean he’s on the verge of seeing his wish come true? My happiness, my Father’s happiness…

“I have no intention of returning to my original world with such a bad aftertaste, though. It’s because of me—the Hero—that things turned out this way. It’s not that I’m taking responsibility… but I want to use the time I have left for the sake of the survivors.”
Father said this with a serious expression. It resembled the expression he showed at the end of the last loop. He must have made up his mind. As for me… what should I do?
“Motoyasu-kun.”
“Yes?”
“Earlier, I sort of told you to choose ‘No,’ but I want you to decide for yourself, Motoyasu-kun.”
“…Why is that?”
“We’ve taken on too much. I think it would be incredibly painful to erase all the time we’ve spent with the people we’ve walked alongside so far, as if it never happened.”

I hadn’t thought about it until now, but it’s true—I’ve looped countless times and met so many people, including my Father and Filolial-sama. And with every loop, I’ve reset everything. Until now, the loops were forced upon me, but this time, I have a choice.
